official.title: Postdoc in Ocean - Sea Ice Interactions
official.description_text:
Deploy detailed models of coupled ocean / sea ice processes, probe their turbulent interactions, compare with observations, and design parameterizations for global climate models.
Job description
The past decades have been associated with substantial losses of sea ice over both hemispheres. Existing climate models are currently unable to accurately forecast these changes, in part due to their imperfect representation of ocean and sea ice interactions at sub-grid scales.
This project aims to improve our physical understanding of these fine-scale processes, including the melting and breakage of sea ice, using a framework consisting of an ocean Large Eddy Simulation (LES) and a Discrete Element Model (DEM) of sea ice. Results from these simulations will be validated against a combination of in-situ and remote sensing data from both the Arctic and Antarctic sea ice regions. Based on this new understanding, the candidate will develop parameterizations that can emulate these physics for use in more coarsely-resolved climate models.
This fully-funded position is part of the European Research Council (ERC) 'ICE-FLOE' project, and will involve collaborations with other team members at TU Delft and internationally. There may also be the opportunity to assist with a research cruise in Antarctica.
Job requirements
PhD in oceanography, cryospheric science, climate science, or atmospheric science.
Experience with Large Eddy Simulations, turbulence research, and the Julia programming language is an advantage but not required.
Interest in the intersection of solid/fluid mechanics.
Ability to work independently.
Excellent command of written and spoken English.
Ability to start the position in January-March 2027 (with some flexibility).

You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.
Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences
The Faculty of Civil Engineering & Geosciences (CEG) is committed to outstanding international research and education in the field of civil engineering, applied earth sciences, traffic and transport, water technology, and delta technology. Our research feeds into our educational programmes and covers societal challenges such as climate change, energy transition, resource availability, urbanisation and clean water. Our research projects are conducted in close cooperation with a wide range of research institutions. CEG is convinced of the importance of open science and supports its scientists in integrating open science in their research practice. The Faculty of CEG comprises 28 research groups in the following seven departments: Materials Mechanics Management & Design, Engineering Structures, Geoscience and Engineering, Geoscience and Remote Sensing, Transport & Planning, Hydraulic Engineering and Water Management.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position in computational oceanography and cryospheric science, developing coupled ocean-sea ice Large Eddy Simulation and Discrete Element Models to improve climate model parameterizations. Work involves turbulence research, model validation against observational data, and potential Antarctic fieldwork within an ERC-funded climate science project.

thematic_fit.rationale: The position is rooted in climate science, computational fluid dynamics, and physical oceanography. The researcher's expertise is in human-centred XR, collaborative learning systems, and spatial cognition—fundamentally different knowledge domains. Mentions of 'modelling' and 'simulations' are superficial overlap; the actual research problem (ocean-ice physics, turbulence, parameterization for climate models) has no thematic connection to immersive learning or human-computer interaction.

methodological_fit.rationale: Both domains value computational modelling and empirical validation. However, the researcher's methodological strength is in experimental user studies, qualitative/quantitative evaluation of human behaviour and learning outcomes, and design-science research. This position requires advanced numerical simulation, turbulence physics, and remote sensing data interpretation—skills not present in the profile. The validation here is against geophysical observations, not human performance measures.

growth_value.rationale: Accepting this position would require a complete pivot away from human-centred XR toward physical science and climate modelling. While learning new computational tools (Julia, LES frameworks) is possible, it does not close gaps relevant to the researcher's target identity (spatial understanding, collaborative immersive systems, learning science). The research questions and methodologies are orthogonal to future HCI/XR goals.

strategic_value.rationale: TU Delft is in a priority geography (Netherlands, Europe) and is research-intensive. However, the Faculty (Civil Engineering & Geosciences) and research group (oceanography/climate) are outside the researcher's target network. The ERC funding is stable but the postdoc does not position the researcher for future doctoral or faculty pathways in human-centred XR or HCI. Moving into climate science would require years to build credibility in that domain.

eligibility_flags: Requires completed PhD by start date (January–March 2027); researcher holds MSc by Research (in progress). Ineligible unless thesis is submitted and conferred before employment.

Posting requests 'PhD in oceanography, cryospheric science, climate science, or atmospheric science'—researcher's MSc is in Creative Multimedia. Strong disciplinary mismatch may disqualify application.
Experience with Large Eddy Simulations and Julia are listed as advantages; researcher has neither.
risks: Fundamental career misalignment: accepting this role would establish the researcher as a climate/oceanography postdoc, making future transitions to HCI/XR significantly harder.
Credential gap: MSc in Creative Multimedia does not meet the stated PhD field requirements. Application may be rejected before evaluation.
Skill reset required: no transferable expertise in LES, climate modelling, or geophysical data analysis. Learning curve is steep and extended.

Target identity conflict: this position moves the researcher away from all core themes (human-centred XR, collaborative systems, spatial learning, wayfinding). It does not advance doctoral or faculty pathways in HCI.

eligibility_reasons: whether a completed degree is required before employment is not stated; your MSc is still in progress — verify with the source
